title: Own It #1: the page that jumped

fields.title: The page that jumped
fields.subtitle: A failed UAT, reviewed by a blunt AI skill. Then fixed, and measured.

beats.say: UAT came back bad. The product list jumps while it loads, and the team has reasons.

fields.title: “It worked on my machine.”
fields.body: The QA API is slow. The testers clicked too fast. Nobody uses the site on train wifi.

beats.say: The API is slow. The testers clicked too fast. It worked on my machine.
Here is the page on a slow phone connection, with every layout shift outlined.
Grey blocks first. Then the real cards arrive, taller, and shove everything down.
Then each picture lands and pushes the cards below it again.
And the font swaps in late, so every title and price moves one more time.

scenes.prompt: UAT came back bad on the product list. The notes are in uat/feedback.md and what the team said is in uat/excuses.md. Do an after-action review.

beats.say: So we hand it to after-action, a free skill inspired by Extreme Ownership.
REWRITE FROM THE REAL RUN: what it read before it judged.
REWRITE FROM THE REAL RUN: the blunt reality, in its own words.
Fix one: the skeleton uses the card's own layout, one placeholder per product.
Fix two: every image gets its size before it arrives.
Fix three: the banner gets a slot that is always there.
Fix four: preload the font, and never swap it in late.
Measured with Lighthouse on a throttled phone, before and after.

fields.title: LCP went up. The page did not get slower.
fields.body: The pictures arrive at the same moment in both builds. Now the largest thing on screen is a product image, not the heading. That is the next episode.

beats.say: One honest note. The load metric went up, but the page did not get slower. The biggest thing on screen is now a real product image, and that is the next fight.
